column1: # gate-coverage.tsv — what the cc-harness gate COVERS, declared.
# monitor/cc-harness/gate.sh to print its coverage boundary beside the
#   3 pane_states   comma-separated pane-state states this scenario
#                   ASSERTS, or `-`. Every member must be in
#                   appear as a token in the scenario file (checked, and
#                   deliberately a PERMISSIVE falsifier — it catches an
#                   invented claim, it does not verify a true one).
#   4 delivery      comma-separated delivery transports this scenario
#                   DRIVES, or `-`. Members must be declared by a
#   5 note          free text. REQUIRED and non-empty for kind=exempt, AND
#                   for kind=exempt it must additionally carry an OWNER: a
#                   An exemption nobody had to justify is an omission with a
#                   row in front of it — and A REASON IS NOT AN OWNER: this
#                   file's own `apispoof` row satisfied "has a reason" with a
#                   sentence CONCEDING that no rationale was on record. Prose
#                   gives an exemption somewhere to be inherited; a ref or a
#                   date gives it somewhere to be re-argued. Same predicate as
#                   (#1482), deliberately one rule rather than two that drift.
# THE RATCHET: every test-realmodel-*.sh on disk must appear here as
# `gated` or `exempt`, or the gate REFUSES (exit 2). gate.sh has always
# warned that "adding the file without adding this line would have
# reproduced #724 one level down"; this file is what makes that a red
# COLUMN 3/4 VALUES SELECT, they do not merely label: a token written here
# is matched against the derived vocabularies, and an unrecognised one is a
# refusal, not a note (CLAUDE.md, "a field that SELECTS is not a label").

structural select-dialog arm; workspace-trust modal must not classify empty (your-org/nexus-code#896); arms 1b/2b drive the REAL paste-followup.sh against that dialog — it must REFUSE and the pane must SURVIVE, with a delivering control (your-org/nexus-code#1321)
canary: CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED=1 keeps an unseeded workdir off the workspace-trust dialog; control arm proves the gate is live (your-org/nexus-code#1334)

the watcher's EMIT PASTE through the real binary (your-org/nexus-code#1591): drives production main.sh `_paste_to_target_unlocked` -> monitor/_paste-deliver.sh with emit-shaped bodies (collapsed to a pasted-text placeholder) and asserts the version- and flag-agnostic property `reported delivered ==> a request reached the backend AND the transcript recorded it`; arms: ASCII control, a body the 2.1.277 review step HOLDS (recovered by the evidence-gated second Enter), a body normalised before the paste, a paste into a BUSY pane (queued, sent on drain), and a NEGATIVE CONTROL with the Enter withheld so the delivery instrument is shown able to say no. First scenario on the delivery axis.

the ORCHESTRATOR-RESPAWN verify stage through the real binary (your-org/nexus-code#1622): drives production `_respawn_orchestrator` end to end (launcher, kill + new-window, readiness probe, bracketed paste, Enter, post-paste verify) with --force-replace --resume-sid; records every pane-state reading after the readiness probe and asserts none is INDETERMINATE (empty/unknown/none); arms: no fault (one request, one record, one Enter), the paste's Enter DROPPED at the transport (recovered by exactly one verify Enter: one request, one record), and a NEGATIVE arm where an operator draft replaces the paste (rc 4, no request, no record, no Enter).

the dangerous-rm permission prompt that shows even under --dangerously-skip-permissions (your-org/nexus-code#1632): the PRODUCTION monitor/hooks/dangerous-rm-decide.sh wired as a PermissionRequest hook DECIDES it — orchestrator mode denies with a delegate message the model receives; worker mode forwards it, and an answer from the REAL `ng decision-answer` allows (the command ran) or denies (the reason reaches the model), while no answer is a deny well inside the 2-minute countdown. A behaviour-stripped control shows the prompt without the hook; two MUST-NOT-FLIP arms (a non-rm Bash prompt and a Write prompt, both raised by a PreToolUse ask) still render with the worker hook wired and forward nothing. Asserts no pane-state.

the TOOL-PERMISSION dialog (jacob-greene/nexus#157, #158): a worker booted WITHOUT --dangerously-skip-permissions (CCH_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=0) paints real Write and Edit permission dialogs, and pane-state must classify both blocked, never the retire-safe empty; a default-boot arm shows the knob changes nothing else, and an idle-frame negative control shows the dialog assertion can say no

VI-safe paste (GUIDE 2c): editorMode=vim, box dropped to NORMAL mode, then the production respawn brief (`_respawn_paste_prompt_file` through _paste-deliver.sh) and the production follow-up (paste-followup.sh), both bracketed, driven under cch_with_tmux_env with delivery and submit pinned; a plain-paste control proves the marker bytes cannot type themselves, and a final arm pins that a bracketed paste with NO guard still lands (the property that makes the guard redundant)

hook-contract scenario beyond PreToolUse's payload (GUIDE 2d): --settings-wired marker hooks; UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse (matcher alternation selects Bash) and Stop FIRE, and a PreToolUse exit 2 BLOCKS the call (no PostToolUse, asserted behind the Stop barrier); an unwired-marker control; wires no production hook script

EXISTS AND IS NOT GATED, BY MEASUREMENT. OWNER: your-org/nexus-code#1535. The longjob-watch dispatcher is a plugin monitor, and the host arms plugin monitors only when the GrowthBook rollout flag tengu_amber_sentinel (default FALSE at 2.1.272) is served; under the mock backend the binary is a "third-party provider", GrowthBook is off, the disk cache is not consulted and the flag is the default — measured 2026-09-15: four harness boots with --plugin-dir, trust seeded, telemetry re-enabled and the cache seeded, footer 0 monitor and no ledger every time. So this scenario boots, sees no ledger and SKIPS with that reason; the arming, delivery, mid-turn and three-events-no-re-arm claims are measured by the hermetic REAL-AUTH probes recorded on #1535, and the cc-update GUIDE (2g) carries the by-hand recipe. Re-evaluate the moment the harness can boot first-party auth or a local flag override exists (the shipped build stubs readConfigOverrides/getEnvironmentOverrides to nothing).

EXISTS AND IS NOT GATED. 529-spoof StopFailure -> interrupted -> resume chain. OWNER: your-org/nexus-code#1486 — enrolment was never EVALUATED (the #1261 fix made the omission visible rather than deciding it), so the open question is whether this scenario should be gated, not why it is exempt. Tracked there rather than inherited here; it drives _idle_probe.sh, which no gated scenario reaches.

EXISTS AND IS NOT GATED. Multi-turn exchange with injected render distortion through the real _idle_probe.sh engagement bookkeeping. OWNER: your-org/nexus-code#1486 — same unevaluated enrolment as apispoof. It is the closest existing scenario to a delivery-path exercise (it send-keys prompts), which is why the delivery gap below is 0/2 rather than partially covered; #1486 asks whether tmux-paste deserves to be a gate scenario given that it is the transport whose failure archived 75 emits in #1477.

column5: test-realmodel-trust-sandboxed-env.sh drives the CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED=1 canary every launcher this file generates now relies on to stay off the workspace-trust dialog (your-org/nexus-code#1334); the launcher COMPOSITION and the detect-and-recover loop are driven by test-spawn-worker-trust-verify.sh (unit), not through the real binary -- so this row speaks for the flag's semantics, not for the script
every classification scenario asserts pane-state's verdict on real harness bytes (idle/busy/absent, blocked, autosuggest, over-limit, user-typing, trust dialog)

the dispatcher cannot be armed under the mock backend (GrowthBook off → tengu_amber_sentinel default false, see the exempt test-realmodel-longjob-wake.sh row), so no gated scenario drives it through the real binary; its emit policy, probes, caps and the launch-path arming are driven by test-longjob-watch.sh, test-longjob-plugin-arming.sh and test-pane-state-longjob-discount.sh (unit), and the real-binary wake is measured by hermetic real-auth probes (your-org/nexus-code#1535)

the OVERLAY GUARD half: test-realmodel-trust-dialog.sh arms 1b/2b run the real script against the real trust dialog (refuses, names the overlay, stamps nothing, pane survives) and against the idle control (a --no-enter paste lands) — your-org/nexus-code#1321. also the bracketed PASTE + SUBMIT, from test-realmodel-vipaste.sh in VI normal mode. NOT the whole delivery path: CONFIRM through the real binary is still driven by no gated scenario (a harness window has no heartbeat or transcript for it to read), which is why the delivery axis above stays 0/2 and monitor/send.sh stays a known-gap

test-realmodel-auth-failure-hooks.sh wires the REAL writer (and the REAL stamp-clear.sh) as the StopFailure/Stop hooks of the real binary against a 401 mock, and asserts the marker it writes for the orchestrator env: category=auth recovery=operator, cleared by a successful turn (your-org/nexus-code#1520, #1548 F1)

test-realmodel-dangerous-rm-decide.sh wires the REAL hook into the real binary in both modes and asserts each outcome through the tool result the model received: orchestrator deny, answer-driven worker allow/deny through the real `ng decision-answer`, timeout deny, and must-not-flip arms that still prompt; the predicate, the verb refusals, the self-answer and nonce checks, and the watcher row are driven by test-dangerous-rm-decide-hook.sh (unit) (your-org/nexus-code#1632)

test-realmodel-pretooluse-hook.sh asserts the PreToolUse payload FIELDS the hook reads, not the hook's own verdicts; the guard is driven by test-bash-footgun-guard.sh (unit), never through the real binary
no gated scenario drives a delivery transport through the real binary (the delivery axis above reads 0/2 for the same reason)
exercised only by EXEMPT scenarios (apispoof, long-exchange); a gated classification scenario stops at pane-state
test-realmodel-trust-dialog.sh mentions it but asserts the pane-state classification of the modal, not an unstick action through the real binary

test-realmodel-paste-held.sh drives the confirmed-delivery primitive end to end against the real binary: normalise, bracketed paste from a file, Enter, transcript confirmation, and the evidence-gated second Enter on a HELD prompt (your-org/nexus-code#1591)

test-realmodel-paste-held.sh evals `_paste_to_target_unlocked` straight out of production main.sh and drives it into a real pane; the rest of main.sh (compose, dedup, scheduling) is NOT driven by any gated scenario
